_: WM_CLAIMS — the structured form of all 34 ability blurbs. ⚠️ THIS FILE IS A TEMPORARY SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH. These declarations belong in `src/game/rules.ts` beside the `desc:` they describe (`AbilityBlurb.claims`), for the same reason `AbilityBlurb.weapon` lives there: a blurb and its claims that can drift apart WILL. They are here only because `rules.ts` was owned by another agent when this gate was built. See wm_gate.mjs's header for the migration. Every `span` must be an exact substring of the blurb — that is what makes an edited blurb a RED GATE rather than a silent divergence.
_thresholdNote: The one judgement threshold is 3000 ms, declared in wm_vocab.mjs and read in BOTH directions: `stun-few-seconds` (>= 3000 ms) and `stun-brief` (< 3000 ms) are exact complements over the stun weapons, so a stun card cannot be made true by DELETING its duration clause — only by describing the duration it has. Everything else is a field test or a roster percentile. 🔴 Do not move the threshold to turn a card green; move the card. See rules.ts beside STUN_DURATION_MS and DECISIONS §81.

donut.Candy.desc: Throws candies that chip away health
donut.Candy.why: "candies" is a BARE PLURAL and is read as flavour, not as a pellet count — see wm_gate's plural rule. The weapon does fire 3 pellets, which shows up as an UNDECLARED mechanic rather than as a pass.

donut.~Sticky Trail.desc: Leaves a filling trail - hurts enemies, speeds him up

taco.Filling.desc: Throws his filling for heavy damage

taco.Double.desc: Special: throws filling and onion together for massive damage

burrito.Disc.desc: Throws himself like a flying disc for damage
burrito.Disc.why: "like a" makes this a SIMILE, so it is read as flavour rather than as a claim that the fighter itself is displaced. JUDGEMENT CALL — the literal reading would be a MISSING `self-launch` (there is no sim-side dash; `movement.ts:365` says knockback is visual-only).

burrito.Roll.desc: Rolls up and freezes enemies in place for a moment

burrito.Swarm.desc: Special: squeezes out all his toppings, which fly everywhere and chase enemies dealing damage - the flying toppings can be destroyed
c: the flying toppings can be destroyed

egg.Tackle.desc: Launches herself at the enemy for big damage - slow to charge up
egg.Tackle.why: "slow to charge up" is read as RECHARGE (cooldown 2200ms, top third), not as a wind-up — this weapon has no `castMs`. JUDGEMENT CALL: if DECISIONS §77-§80 convert this ultimate, the claim upgrades to `wind-up` and this line must change with it.

egg.Hatch.desc: She cracks open and a chick bursts out, pecking for damage
c: cracks open and a chick bursts out

egg.Shards.desc: Broken shell pieces slow enemies and chip away their health
egg.Shards.why: "pieces" is a bare plural, so the pellet count is not read as a claim. The weapon does fire 3.

lollipop.Smash.desc: Swings herself like a hammer for heavy damage
lollipop.Smash.why: "like a hammer" is a SIMILE and is read as flavour, on the same rule as burrito.Disc.

lollipop.Giant.desc: Grows huge and slams the widest area in the game, making everyone dizzy
c: slams the widest area in the game

pizza.Dough.desc: Throws dough balls that slow enemies down
pizza.Dough.why: "dough balls" is a bare plural, so the pellet count is not read as a claim. STRICT READING: this weapon fires ONE projectile, so a plural-as-pellets rule would make it a WRONG VALUE.

pizza.Tomato.desc: Tomatoes stick to the floor, damaging and slowing anyone who steps on them
c: slowing anyone who steps on them

pizza.Cheese.desc: Cheese sticks to an enemy's face and blocks their vision until someone hits them
c: Cheese sticks to an enemy's face
pizza.Cheese.why: This card never mentions the stun the weapon actually applies, so `stun` shows up as an UNDECLARED mechanic — the blurb and the record describe two different weapons.

sushi.Rice.desc: Throws a spray of rice grains - each one chips away a little health
c: each one chips away a little health

sushi.Seaweed.desc: Seaweed lures every enemy toward it while he shoots them
sushi.Seaweed.why: The weapon carries a `slow` the card never mentions — UNDECLARED.

sushi.Fish.desc: Turns into a pile of fish that attack for small damage
c: Turns into a pile of fish that attack
sushi.Fish.why: "Turns into a pile of fish" is read as flavour for a melee swing. STRICT READING: a transformation is a mechanic the sim has no state for, which would make this a MISSING MECHANIC.

sushi.Catch.desc: Special: throws seaweed with fish - the fish grow huge and the seaweed scatters in a fan, pulling enemies everywhere
c: the seaweed scatters in a fan

soup.Splash.desc: Throws his soup liquid - each splash chips away a little health

soup.Noodle.desc: Throws noodles that slow enemies down

soup.Dump.desc: Special: tips himself over onto an enemy, pouring all his soup and noodles - big damage and a heavy slow
c: tips himself over onto an enemy, pouring all his soup and noodles

waterbottle.Spray.desc: Sprays water that slows enemies down a lot
waterbottle.Spray.why: `pellets: 3` is UNDECLARED — the card reads as one stream.

waterbottle.Glass.desc: Shoots glass shards that deal damage and freeze enemies

waterbottle.Cap.desc: Fires his cap - enemies slip when it hits

waterbottle.Mega.desc: Special: launches himself up (takes a few seconds), his cap becomes a second bottle, and together they become one giant bottle that dumps water on an enemy for huge damage and a heavy slow
c: his cap becomes a second bottle
together they become one giant bottle

hotdog.Mustard.why: JUDGEMENT CALL — "Burns" is read as flavour for damage on a mustard weapon, not as a damage-over-time claim. There is no DoT in the sim; the literal reading would make this a MISSING mechanic.

hotdog.Ketchup.desc: Makes enemies slide and lose control
hotdog.Ketchup.why: "slide" is read as the slow. "lose control" is separate and has no mechanic: `movement.ts:365` records that knockback is visual-only and that a dash or a pull would be new.
